- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment alternates between bullish/bearish (e.g., 0.33/1.00 cycles), model exhibits lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact; cap forecast growth rate at 0.5% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., 0.00/0.33), model often fails to anticipate sharp drops; add 1–3% downward buffer to forecast mean.
